_note: The scenario pack. `dev/scripts/viz/build.py` runs each `argv` verbatim and refuses
to publish a page whose run stopped matching the `expect_*` fields. That is the
whole point of the file: a pinned seed is only meaningful as (commit, seed, flags),
so every number a narration says out loud is pinned here and machine-checked on
every build. A scenario that quietly changes behaviour fails the build instead of
shipping a stale claim (the failure commit 1e80be3 already fixed once).
Every vopr `argv` carries `--recheck-every 0`, and it is load-bearing rather than
tidy. The determinism recheck re-executes a seed whenever `seed % --recheck-every`
is 0 (default 10), and the two executions are not symmetric on the page: the trace
brackets ONE of them, while the terminal's reach table is process-cumulative and
counts BOTH. A reader who pasted the command a page printed therefore saw every
oracle count and every merge-evidence count at exactly twice the page's figure.
Disabling the recheck makes the traced run the only execution, so page and terminal agree
number for number. The `determinism` scenario is the deliberate exception — it sets
`--recheck-every 1` because the double execution is its subject — and it carries a
caveat saying so.
status: live      built and verified on every run
retired   a finding that has been adjudicated away; not run, shown as closed
pending   its producer does not exist yet; build.py fails once `needs` appears
may_skip             the named local dependency may be absent, and then the page is not
built and says so on the index instead of failing the build
expect_event_kinds   event types that must all appear, or the recording measures nothing
expect_exit          the process exit code (0 clean, 2 invariant violation, 3 determinism, 4 reach gate)
expect_violation     substring every violation line must contain, or null for a clean run
expect_trace_events  summary.trace_events — the determinism hasher's record count, which is
the admitted storage ops PLUS one tuple per CAS outcome. NOT the number
a narration means by `storage ops`; that one is expect_event_counts.op
expect_event_counts  per-event-type line counts in the JSONL
expect_acks          the ack split, because `acks` is three numbers: `answered` (every upload
and delete the workload issued), `accepted`/`refused` (whether the server
took it), and `distinct_files_acked` (filenames the ledger holds an
accepted upload for — the `N acked` verdict pill on the page)
expect_world         objects left at quiescence, folded from the `world` deltas by build.py.
`quarantine` counts OBJECTS, `distinct_quarantined_bodies` counts
BYTE-SETS; a narration saying `preserved bodies` means the second
expect_oracles       per-oracle `verdict` the page must render: `held`, `violated` or
`not-executed`, keyed by the REACH_METER label
expect_counts        graph producers only: keys read straight out of the payload's `counts`

scenarios.title: One filename, two bodies, three regions
scenarios.narration: Two writers publish different bytes under the same immutable filename in three regions, and 921 storage ops later the filename is frozen in all three while both byte-sets are still on disk — two distinct bodies, kept as four _quarantine/ copies across the three regions. The fleet refuses to pick a winner and refuses to lose one.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

Byte identity here is per key: the three buckets agree on truth and views, and deliberately do not agree on their own bucket-local state (`_state/`, `.origin` stamps) or on which quarantined copies they hold.

scenarios.title: The smallest world that can conflict
scenarios.narration: Two nodes, two regions, one filename, sixteen workload ops: in 588 storage ops the contested name is fenced with .frozen on both sides and the losing body is kept under _quarantine/ rather than overwritten.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.
Which merge verdicts a seed presents is not pinned here — only the evidence left at quiescence is. The fence and the preserved body are the claim; the route to them is the simulator's business.

scenarios.title: Same seed, writes pinned to one region: the merge algebra never runs
scenarios.narration: Three nodes, two regions, every write homed to the same region: 980 storage ops, four uploads accepted over four distinct filenames with nothing refused, and not one .frozen fence or _quarantine/ body is ever created.
caveats: This is the control run. Its partner `dead-code-partitioned` is the same seed and the same topology with one flag added; the player plays the two side by side and does not diff them.

scenarios.title: Same seed. One flag. The merge algebra wakes up
scenarios.narration: Add --partition 100 and nothing else: the same seed now runs 1,166 storage ops and leaves four .frozen fences and four preserved bodies — held as five _quarantine/ copies, one of them a second region's copy of a body another region also kept — where the aligned run left none.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

The chip row's two op numbers are both true and they are not the same measurement: `1,166 storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, and `1,167 hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome. The binary's own summary line prints the second figure, under the name `storage-op interleavings`.
The aligned twin is a separate run of the same seed. Two panels, one clock, no diff engine.

scenarios.title: The multi-region nightly profile, one seed
scenarios.narration: The nightly's multi-region profile plus --partition 100 on a single seed: 2,249 storage ops; 21 client requests answered, of which 12 were accepted (10 uploads over 9 distinct filenames — the 9 the verdict pill counts — and two deletes) and 9 were deletes the server refused; six .frozen fences; seven preserved bodies held as eight _quarantine/ copies; and every oracle that executed held.
caveats: `--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

The chip row's two op numbers are both true and they are not the same measurement: `2,249 storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, and `2,252 hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome. The binary's own summary line prints the second figure, under the name `storage-op interleavings`, which is why the command above reports 2252 where this page says 2,249.
One seed is a sample, not the nightly. The per-oracle execution counts on this page are this seed's own; the nightly's are in dev/TESTING.md.

scenarios.title: Run the same seed twice and compare everything
scenarios.narration: Every other page on this index is a pinned seed, which is only evidence if it replays. Here that is the subject: --recheck-every 1 re-executes seed 21 from nothing once the first run finishes and compares the whole storage-op sequence and the final world hash against it — the same 1,042 storage ops in the same order, the same two .frozen fences, the same three preserved bodies. The DETERMINISM oracle is the one asserting it, and it holds.
caveats: This is the one page in the pack whose printed command runs the seed TWICE, so read the two side by side with care: every count on this page is ONE execution, while the terminal's reach table and merge-evidence table are process-cumulative and cover BOTH. The command reports DURABILITY 4 where the page reads 2, and six `_quarantine/<pkg>/<file>@sha` objects where the page's world holds three. DETERMINISM is the exception in the other direction — it fires once per seed, so it reads 1 in both. Every other vopr page in this pack passes `--recheck-every 0`, which disables the recheck entirely and makes page and terminal agree number for number.

The chip row's two op numbers are both true and they are not the same measurement: `1,042 storage ops traced` counts the gated storage calls, and `1,045 hashed trace events` is what the determinism hash covers — the same calls plus one record per compare-and-set outcome. The binary's own summary line prints the second figure, under the name `storage-op interleavings`.

What the oracle compares is the op trace and a hash of the final world, not the recording: the second execution is not traced. A nondeterminism that produced identical calls and identical final bytes by a different internal route would pass.
`--partition N` homes each node's *writes* to one bucket. Reads, sweeps, audits and oracles are not partitioned.

scenarios.title: A download a client would reject, and everything else green
scenarios.narration: We repoint one sidecar at a digest no stored body has, and of the 23 oracle slots exactly one fires — SELF_CONSISTENCY, which is the check a real client performs when it hashes the file it was handed against the index it read.
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break attest`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.
One bucket, so the cross-region oracles (CONVERGENCE, ACK_TOTALITY) do not execute on this run and render as "not executed".

scenarios.title: The oracle that refuses to settle
scenarios.narration: We plant one _repl/ object no sweep recognizes, so no fixpoint exists: the heal loop grinds through all twelve rounds and 221 drain passes instead of the usual two, then refuses to call the fleet settled.
caveats: The defect is injected by `--break wedge`, not produced by the product. This is a mutation test proving the oracle can fire — not a bug found in the wild.
Twelve rounds is the whole budget (`HEAL_ROUNDS`). A green run of this profile uses two or three; dev/TESTING.md records the worst seed ever measured at three of twelve.

scenarios.title: The freeze nobody could justify
scenarios.narration: Seed 1327 froze a filename fleet-wide with only one byte-set attested for it — the last open finding with a millisecond repro, closed at 439b839.
scenarios.retired_because: Adjudicated: `fix: a freeze whose evidence a racing delete erased read as unjustified` (439b839). The seed now exits 0 and prints FREEZE_JUSTIFIED. It was an oracle bug, not a product bug, so there is nothing left to show — and a page that still called it open would be exactly the stale evidence this pack exists to prevent.

scenarios.title: Every interleaving of two writers racing one filename
scenarios.narration: The exhaustive state space of two private uploads of the same immutable filename into different regions — 80 states, 178 transitions, 99 of them joins where independent orders reconverge on the same world.

scenarios.title: The _dirty/ marker protocol, drawn in full at a reduced size
scenarios.narration: Every interleaving of one upload, one delete and one worker tick over the _dirty/ intent-and-commit markers — 758 states, 1,455 transitions — beside the 1,497,544-state configuration CI checks on every merge and nobody can draw.

scenarios.title: The region a node reads from goes dark
scenarios.narration: Reads fall back to the write region in seconds, the write pin never moves, a real uv pip install keeps working, and reads return only once that region is healthy and owes nothing.

scenarios.title: The preferred region goes dark; reads stay in their region
scenarios.narration: The fleet-wide write home goes dark while this node reads from a different region: new writes move to the next healthy region in preference order and the node's reads never leave home.

scenarios.title: How much of this has actually been run
scenarios.narration: Every figure on this page carries the file and line it was measured at — and the commit, wherever the source records one; the build refuses to publish a figure without a source. The two live rows are re-measured on this machine at build time.
